run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T13:28:09Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on service otel-demo/frontend-proxy is explained by a short, dense burst of failed checkout traffic at ~13:29-13:31Z, not by a fault inside frontend-proxy. frontend-proxy's ingress spans recorded 78 error spans in the 13:29:00-13:30:00 bucket and 42 in 13:30:00-13:31:00 (out of 1414 and 1304 ingress spans respectively), with matching egress errors (78 and 40); outside those two minutes its ingress error series shows only ~2 per minute. In exactly those minutes, checkout recorded 44 errors on both oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and its outbound oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge, frontend recorded 74 then 44 errors on POST /api/checkout and on its grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder client span, and payment's own charge / grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge span rate dropped to 0 for two consecutive minutes (48-90/min before, 60-92/min after). The only change in namespace otel-demo in that interval is Deployment payment being rollout-restarted at 13:28:26Z: a new ReplicaSet payment-7b6bfb9fb4 carrying kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-16T13:28:26Z with a pod template identical to payment-55766d76b9 (same image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment, same env and resources), and the old pod payment-55766d76b9-cpgm4 was deleted at 13:28:29Z. The replacement pod was marked Ready at 13:28:29Z even though the payment container declares no readiness, liveness or startup probe and its application logged "payment gRPC server started on port 8080" only at 13:29:40.877Z, with the first "Charge request received." at 13:30:18.929Z; the Deployment runs 1 replica with RollingUpdate 25%/25%. With no readiness gate, the rollout removed the only serving payment pod before its replacement actually listened, so CheckoutService/PlaceOrder failed, frontend's /api/checkout errored, and frontend-proxy counted those failures. A separate residual error source also exists: frontend-proxy ingress errors of ~2 per minute at 13:19, 13:20, 13:28, 13:34, 13:36 and 13:40, i.e. before and long after the burst, whose trace-level detail is not citable in this Run. Caveats: the alerting rule definition and the stated value 0.01111111111111111 could not be read or reproduced, and Jaeger retained no traces after ~13:16:34Z, so the HTTP status codes of the burst responses themselves are unobserved.

claims.text: frontend-proxy recorded 78.22 ingress error spans and 59.94 "router frontend egress" error spans in a whole-window increase over 2026-11-16T12:28:33Z-13:49:33Z, against 24092.44 and 24108.70 STATUS_CODE_UNSET spans on the same span names, so error spans exist on frontend-proxy's own ingress and egress spans.

The errors concentrate in two minute buckets: frontend-proxy ingress ERROR increase = 78 at the 13:30:00Z evaluation and 42 at 13:31:00Z, and "router frontend egress" ERROR = 78 and 40 at the same two evaluations, while the same ingress series shows only 2 errors per minute at 13:28:00Z, 13:34:00Z, 13:36:00Z and 13:40:00Z and egress ERROR is 0 outside the burst.

Per-minute ingress volume on frontend-proxy: 1336 STATUS_CODE_UNSET + 78 ERROR spans at 13:30:00Z and 1262 UNSET + 42 ERROR at 13:31:00Z, versus baseline minutes such as 1420 UNSET + 2 ERROR at 13:28:00Z or 1456 UNSET + 2 ERROR at 13:32:00Z.

In the same two minutes the failures line up with the checkout path: frontend spans POST, POST /api/checkout, "executing api route (pages) /api/checkout" and grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder each recorded 74 ERROR at 13:30:00Z and 44 ERROR at 13:31:00Z, while checkout recorded 44 ERROR on oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and 44 ERROR on oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge at 13:31:00Z and 0 UNSET PlaceOrder spans in the 13:29:00-13:30:00 bucket.

payment's own serving activity has a two-minute hole: the "charge" and "grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge" span increases are 0 at the 13:30:00Z and 13:31:00Z evaluations, while they are 48-90 per minute before (e.g. 76 at 13:29:00Z) and 60-92 per minute after (77.83 at 13:32:00Z, 92 at 13:34:00Z).

Deployment payment was rollout-restarted at 2026-11-16T13:28:26Z: the new ReplicaSet payment-7b6bfb9fb4 carries the pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-16T13:28:26Z and is identical to the old payment-55766d76b9 in image (ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment), environment variables and resource limits, i.e. a configuration-only restart with an unchanged image.

The replacement sequence is recorded in namespace otel-demo: ReplicaSet payment-7b6bfb9fb4 "Created pod: payment-7b6bfb9fb4-fwlht" at 13:28:26Z, Deployment payment "Scaled up replica set payment-7b6bfb9fb4 from 0 to 1" at 13:28:26Z, pod payment-7b6bfb9fb4-fwlht Scheduled 13:28:26Z and Started container payment 13:28:29Z, and old pod payment-55766d76b9-cpgm4 "Stopping container payment" / ReplicaSet "Deleted pod: payment-55766d76b9-cpgm4" at 13:28:29Z with "Scaled down replica set payment-55766d76b9 from 1 to 0" at 13:28:29Z.

The replacement pod payment-7b6bfb9fb4-fwlht reached Ready=True and ContainersReady=True at 2026-11-16T13:28:29Z (immediately at container start), has restartCount 0 and an empty lastState, is owned by ReplicaSet payment-7b6bfb9fb4, and declares no readinessProbe, livenessProbe or startupProbe.

The restarted payment application only began listening well after the pod was marked Ready: its first log line in the window is "payment gRPC server started on port 8080" at 2026-11-16T13:29:40.877Z, and the first "Charge request received." is at 2026-11-16T13:30:18.929Z; the container emitted no lines between the 13:28:20Z-13:29:30Z probe of its log and the 13:29:40.877Z startup line.

Deployment payment runs replicas 1 under strategy RollingUpdate with maxSurge 25% / maxUnavailable 25%, revision 2, observedGeneration 2, so the restart replaced the only payment pod and no second replica existed to absorb the roughly 71-second application start.

Once the restarted payment application was listening it served charges normally: its log shows repeated "Charge request received." / "Transaction complete." pairs from 13:30:18Z onward (sampled 13:35:23Z-13:35:57Z, all completed), and checkout's own log for 13:35:15Z-13:38:39Z contains repeated "payment went through" lines with no error lines among the 1135 lines matched by that filter.

payment's own spans show no error status: over 12:28:33Z-13:49:33Z the only status labels returned for payment's "charge" and "grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge" spans are STATUS_CODE_UNSET (1211.01 and 1210.82 spans), with no STATUS_CODE_ERROR series for those two span names, whereas zero-valued STATUS_CODE_ERROR series do appear for payment's GET, dns.lookup, tcp.connect, tls.connect and flagd spans. This argues against payment returning an application-level error and for payment being unreachable during the gap.

checkout's outbound PaymentService/Charge p90 duration rose during the burst to 251.67 ms (13:31:00Z sample) and 338 ms (13:34:00Z sample) from 34-86 ms in the preceding samples, and payment's server-side Charge p90 shows isolated high samples of 62.69 ms (13:34:00Z) and 27.33 ms (13:35:00Z) against ~1.9 ms otherwise, consistent with gRPC reconnection after the endpoint change.

Frontend-proxy ingress errors are not confined to the payment-restart burst: the ingress ERROR series is 2 at 13:28:00Z, 2 at 13:34:00Z, 2 at 13:36:00Z and 2 at 13:40:00Z, i.e. a residual trickle of about 2 error spans per minute before and long after the burst.
Cluster-level infrastructure was not degraded: all 5 nodes report Ready=True with MemoryPressure, DiskPressure and PIDPressure all False, and each has 4 allocatable CPUs and about 16 GiB of memory.

frontend-proxy and its callers were not restarted: frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-q5c94, checkout-5dccddf8bb-c4dqt and frontend-675fd7b5c5-sn9gc all show phase Running, restartCount 0, ready true and start times between 12:55:26Z and 12:55:28Z, while payment-7b6bfb9fb4-fwlht is the only pod in otel-demo with a 13:28:26Z start time.

Other services' error series in the same 15-minute view at 13:40:00Z are tiny and on unrelated operations: fraud-detection flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream 1.03, ad flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream 1.03 and recommendation /flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream 2.07, while the checkout-path errors dominate (frontend POST /api/checkout 61.03, frontend grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 61.03, checkout oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge 23.33, frontend-proxy ingress 68.28 and egress 61.03).

Main explanation: the rollout restart of Deployment payment at 13:28:26Z removed the only payment endpoint while the replacement application was still starting (gRPC server up 13:29:40.877Z, first charge served 13:30:18.929Z, no payment Charge spans in the 13:29-13:31 windows). Checkout's oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge calls therefore errored, oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder failed, frontend's POST /api/checkout errored, and frontend-proxy counted those failures on its ingress/egress spans, pushing its request error rate above zero. The 25%/25% RollingUpdate plus the absence of any readiness probe on the payment container allowed the old pod to be removed at 13:28:29Z before the new process listened.

Second, independent contributor: the residual ~2 ingress errors per minute on frontend-proxy at 13:19, 13:20, 13:28, 13:34, 13:36 and 13:40 occur outside the payment burst, so the payment restart cannot explain them. Because the alert is reported as firing above 0, this trickle can keep the error rate nonzero on its own; its cause is not established by the citable evidence in this Run, and the specific upstream failure mode of these requests is unknown.

Rejected: frontend-proxy's own pod or configuration caused the errors. Its pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-q5c94 has run since 12:55:28Z with restartCount 0, and during the burst its ingress and egress error counts move together (78/78 and 42/40) while the failures match frontend's own POST /api/checkout and checkout's PlaceOrder/Charge error spans minute-for-minute.

Rejected: node resource pressure or a node-level fault caused the burst. All five nodes are Ready with no MemoryPressure, DiskPressure or PIDPressure conditions, and the frontend-proxy, frontend and checkout pods show unchanged status while only payment's pod was replaced.

Give the payment container a readiness probe (or startupProbe) on its gRPC port that only passes once the server listens, so the Deployment stops marking the pod Ready at container start while the application needs about 71 seconds to bind port 8080, and consider running more than one payment replica or setting maxUnavailable 0 so a rollout never removes the only payment endpoint.

Verify the RequestErrorRate rule (expression, ratio window, threshold and 'for' duration) in the Prometheus/Alertmanager instance that emitted the alert, since the rule could not be found or read here, and check change/audit history for the kubectl rollout restart of deployment/payment recorded at 13:28:26Z.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate alerting rule is not present in the queried Prometheus: list_prometheus_rules filtered by rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned no rules and an unfiltered listing also returned nothing (status no_data), so the rule's expression, ratio window, threshold and 'for' duration are unknown and the reported value 0.01111111111111111 could not be reproduced from traces_span_metrics_calls_total.

Jaeger retained no traces after about 13:16:34Z in this window, so the HTTP status codes, error details and full span graph of the burst requests at 13:29-13:31Z are unobserved; error-tag and http.status_code=500 searches over 13:29-13:38 returned no data.

The trace-level detail of the residual frontend-proxy errors (upstream status codes and the presence or absence of child frontend spans) appeared only in a sampled Jaeger view covering 13:10:15Z-13:15:10Z that is not citable in this Run, so the failure mode of the residual ~2/min errors remains unknown.
The frontend container's logs could not be read (current instance returned 0 bytes), so the frontend-side error message for the failing POST /api/checkout requests is unknown.
The old payment pod payment-55766d76b9-cpgm4 no longer exists and the replacement container had no previous instance, so the old pod's shutdown behaviour and logs could not be inspected.
Container logs were only readable up to 13:38:36Z (payment) and 13:38:39Z (checkout); anything logged later is unknown.
The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so which actor or automation issued the kubectl rollout restart annotation at 13:28:26Z could not be determined.

rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count returned no series for the window, and http_* / app_* metric names do not exist in this Prometheus (get_metric_names returned no data), so alternative error-rate and latency sources could not be cross-checked.

The PodDisruptionBudget listing returned no objects (status no_data) and no kube_* kube-state-metrics series exist in this Prometheus, so Kubernetes state was observable only as live objects at query time, not as metric history; whether a PDB existed for payment is unknown.

payment-7b6bfb9fb4-fwlht does emit startup and charge lines, but no log line of that container was retained between 13:28:29Z and 13:29:40.877Z, so its exact bind timing and any startup warnings in that gap are unknown.
next_steps: Read the RequestErrorRate rule (expr, window, threshold, for) from the Prometheus that fired it to confirm how the 1.1% figure is computed and which series it uses.

Add a readiness/startup probe to the otel-demo payment container and raise payment replicas or set maxUnavailable 0 so rollouts cannot remove the sole payment endpoint while the app needs about 70 seconds to start listening.
Check audit/change history for the kubectl rollout restart of deployment/payment at 2026-11-16T13:28:26Z and confirm whether it was an intended maintenance action.
Restore or enable frontend container log collection and capture a trace of one residual frontend-proxy ingress error outside the burst to diagnose the remaining sporadic failures.
Check Jaeger ingestion health, since no traces were retained after about 13:16:34Z although span metrics continued to 13:49Z.

Rejected: node resource pressure or a node-level fault caused the burst. All five nodes are Ready with no MemoryPressure, DiskPressure or PIDPressure conditions, and the frontend-proxy, frontend and checkout pods show unchanged status while only payment's pod was replaced.
